contracts.text: Conflicts must be detected for set-set on the same key within the same transaction or merged update when mapConflictPolicy is 'collect' or 'error'.
contracts.adverse_condition: Two or more set operations target the same Y.Map key within a single transaction or merged update, and mapConflictPolicy is 'collect' or 'error'.

contracts.text: Conflicts must be detected for delete-set on the same key within the same transaction or merged update when mapConflictPolicy is 'collect' or 'error'.
contracts.adverse_condition: A delete and a set operation target the same Y.Map key within a single transaction or merged update, and mapConflictPolicy is 'collect' or 'error'.

contracts.text: Conflicts involving Yjs types or subdocs must be marked as ambiguous, either by setting conflict.type to 'ambiguous' or by exposing an ambiguous boolean flag on the conflict object.
contracts.adverse_condition: A detected conflict involves a Yjs type or subdoc value.

contracts.text: When mapConflictPolicy is 'allow', conflicts are neither blocked nor collected, and updates apply normally.
contracts.adverse_condition: mapConflictPolicy is 'allow' and conflicting writes occur.

contracts.text: The mapConflictPolicy is configured via the Y.Doc constructor options as new Y.Doc({ mapConflictPolicy: 'allow' | 'collect' | 'error' }).
In 'error' mode, conflicting map writes throw a MapConflictError.
contracts.adverse_condition: mapConflictPolicy is 'error' and a conflicting map write is detected.

contracts.text: In 'error' mode, merged updates apply atomically with no partial application across all tested conflict types.
contracts.adverse_condition: mapConflictPolicy is 'error' and a merged update containing multiple conflicts across different conflict types is applied.

contracts.text: The thrown MapConflictError must expose an err.conflicts array.
In 'collect' mode, recorded conflicts are accessible via the Y.Doc instance method getMapConflicts().
In 'collect' mode, recorded conflicts are accessible via the Y.Doc instance method getMapConflictSummary().
getMapConflictSummary() returns an object with fields: byType, byKey, byParent, and bySource.
Each field of the summary object (byType, byKey, byParent, bySource) is a plain JavaScript object mapping strings to counts (numbers).
The summary fields support index access such that summary.byType[type] retrieves the count for a given type string.
The summary object must include an overall conflict count, accessible as either count or total.
Each conflict object must include a key field.
Each conflict object must include a parentId field.
Each conflict object must include a type field whose value correctly reflects the classification of the conflict (e.g., set-set, delete-set, or ambiguous for Yjs-type/subdoc conflicts).
Each conflict object must include a source field whose value is one of 'local', 'remote', or 'mixed' and correctly reflects the origin of the conflicting writes.
Each conflict object must include a top-level message field whose value is a string.
Each conflict object must include a writes field whose value is an array.
Each write in the writes array must have a snapshot.summary property whose value is a non-empty string.
Each conflict object must include a resolution object.
The resolution object must include a winner field.
The resolution object must include a strategy field whose value is a string.
The resolution object must include a deterministic field whose value is a boolean.
